description:
FILED s470bj while shipping #996 half A3.  `Pl::ExprToCL::_node_is_definitely_scalar`
answers "provably ONE scalar" for a NUMBER/QUOTE literal and a `$`-sigiled
Symbol leaf and for nothing else -- so an INTERNAL node always answers no,
including the shapes that cannot possibly be a list: a binary arithmetic /
string / comparison operator (its p-op coerces both operands and returns a raw
number or string), an interpolated string (`string_concat`), an anon
array/hash/sub constructor, a single element access (`$h{k}` / `$a[i]` /
`$r->{k}` / `$r->[i]`), a unary `! - + ~`, `++`/`--`, and `\` over one named
container.

s470bj needed exactly that predicate for the `local-push` item licence and did
NOT widen this one, because its only consumer -- `gen_progn_form`'s LIST_CTX
choice between `['vector', @forms]` and `['p-flatten-args', ['list','list',
@forms]]` -- would then change emission across the whole corpus, which is a
separate optimization with its own bar.  The wider predicate lives beside it as
`Pl::ExprToCL::_push_item_is_scalar` (with the pointer here in its comment).

THE ITEM: fold the two into ONE predicate and take the `vector` shape wherever
it now proves out.  `p-flatten-args` allocates a list and walks every operand
at RUNTIME to decide whether to spread it; `(vector ...)` does neither.  Any
list literal with an arithmetic element -- `my @a = ($i*2, $j+1)`, `return
($x.$y, 1)`, `f($i+1, $k)` -- is on the slow shape today.

BAR: a bench row for the shape FIRST (there is none: no standing row builds a
list of computed values in a loop), then corpus-diff with every diff explained,
the full sweep (it is an emission change over a very common shape), and guard
rows for the negatives (a funcall, a slice, a range, `wantarray`, a `do` block
-- everything that CAN be a list must keep flattening).


=== CLOSED (s473r, 2026-09-07) â the shapes it was filed for are ALREADY FAST ===

MEASURED before designing anything.  The task names three shapes as "on the
slow shape today".  All three emit the FAST form on `bfa11c72`:

    my @a = ($i*2, $j+1, $i-$j);
      -> (p-array-= @a (vector (p-* $i 2) (p-+ $j 1) (p-- $i $j)))
    f($i+1, $j*2)
      -> (pl-f (p-+ $i 1) (p-* $j 2))            # no list form at all
    return ($x.$y, 1)
      -> (p-return (p-. $x $y) 1)                # multiple values

CORPUS SCAN (65 files: 45 perl-tests/*.t + 20 lib/**/*.pm, transpiled and the
`(p-flatten-args â¦)` forms extracted and balanced):

    p-flatten-args sites                    182
      of which the @_ construction (%_args)  131   <- not this item at all
      LIST_CTX list forms                     51
      of those, containing NO @ or % sigil     26
      of those 26, an ALL-SCALAR list           1   (perl-tests/eval.t, a
                                                    constant list of strings,
                                                    not in a loop)

The other 25 are `(list "A" (p-list-ctx (p-reverse â¦)))`,
`(p-list-ctx (p-map â¦))` and ranges â genuine LIST producers that MUST
flatten, and which the widened `_node_is_definitely_scalar` would correctly
still refuse.

So the emission change would move ONE site in 65 files, and that site is a
constant list in a test file.  There is no bench row to build for it because
there is no shape to measure.  `_node_is_definitely_scalar` and
`_push_item_is_scalar` stay two predicates; folding them is free of any
measurable prize and would cost the full emission boat (generation bump,
three artifacts, corpus-diff, the full sweep).

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT: a corpus scan (the one above, re-run) that finds a
double-digit number of ALL-SCALAR LIST_CTX flatten sites â i.e. some future
emission change that starts routing computed-scalar lists back through
`p-flatten-args`.  The scanner is `scratch/s473r/scan1141.pl` in the s473r
worktree; it takes a file list and prints the four counts above.
subject: Widen _node_is_definitely_scalar to the operator/constructor shapes local-push already proves (gen_progn_form: `vector` instead of p-flatten-args)
